analysis.title: Global Equity Strategy: 2027 Outlook: Finding Value in Growth
key_insights: GS expects global equities to keep rising in 2027 but with higher volatility: 12-month price targets imply S&P 500 +14%, STOXX 600 +6%, TOPIX +15%, MSCI AP ex Japan +17%, MSCI EM +17%.
2026 was driven by earnings. Returns were similar across regions, reversing the 2009-2025 pattern of US outperformance, and all equity markets de-rated.

Earnings growth is forecast to slow sharply in 2027 as AI capex growth peaks: S&P 500 EPS growth falls from 36% to 11%, Europe from about 18% to 7%, Japan from 24% to 9%, and MSCI AP ex Japan and MSCI EM stay at 26% (GS top-down estimates).

Hyperscaler capex growth is expected to slow, cutting the EPS contribution from capex to S&P 500 growth from 12pp in 2026 to 9pp in 2027 and -5pp in 2028. Consensus IT EPS growth slows from about 89-90% in 2026 to 45% in 2027, and Communication Services from 34% to -5%.

Energy EPS growth is expected to go from 99% in 2026 to about -10% to -11% in 2027 (consensus) as oil prices fall. Basic Materials slows from 45% to 12%. Healthcare is the exception, with consensus EPS growth rising from 4.4% to 17.7%.

Valuations have fallen: the US P/E is 18.5x, down from near the 100th percentile of its 20-year range. Global P/E and PEG ratios are near their 35-year averages. Asia and EM trade well below historical averages.

Global Technology is now in the 20th percentile of its 20-year valuation range and is one of the cheapest sectors on P/E. Hyperscalers trade at 19.7x, below Consumer Staples, and have nearly closed the valuation gap with the other 495 S&P 500 stocks.
GS sees US Hyperscalers as relatively defensive within Growth: the largest companies have turned cash-flow negative, but net debt/equity remains healthy and well below the market's level.

Korea's memory semiconductor sector is pricing a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings, which GS calls excessive given sold-out DRAM and HBM supply through 2029. It trades at 0.7x 2028 P/B, a level that has historically preceded strong returns, but remains highly dependent on AI capex and volatile.

Cost of capital remains elevated. Rates strategists expect a modest tightening cycle and slow progress on cuts in 2027, while credit strategists expect spreads to widen. Bond strategists expect some relief in long-term yields, and the Fed and ECB are expected to move toward cuts in late 2027.

Commodities team forecasts Brent falling from about $100/bbl at end-2026 to $78/bbl at end-2027. This turns the energy impulse from a 0.4pp drag on global growth into a modest boost in 2027 and should lower inflation.

Regional stance on a risk-adjusted basis: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia ex Japan and EM, underweight Europe. Europe is underweight because valuations have not fallen as much as elsewhere, government debt and political risks are higher, and lower oil would reduce earnings growth.

EM concentration is at a record: Korea and Taiwan are about half of MSCI EM, Info Tech is over 40%, and TSMC, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are about 30%. GS sees higher momentum and concentration risk in Asia than in the US.

GS recommends Growth balanced with selective Defensives and beneficiaries of lower oil prices and bond yields, rather than a broad defensive shift. Value has outperformed Growth sharply in recent months, and the Value factor now sits near the 90th percentile of its 20-year valuation range.
Four risks are named: bond volatility, oil volatility, weaker AI capex and momentum/concentration. Each could produce downside or upside.

sector_views.rationale: Valuations have fallen sharply, balance sheets are strong, earnings growth is slower but still strong, and long-duration Growth benefits from lower yields.
Sharp de-rating creates upside, with memory priced for a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings, but volatility stays high and the sector depends on AI capex.
Selective Defensive with reasonable valuations, favored in the US, Asia and EM.
Oil is forecast to fall, putting downward pressure on earnings growth (consensus 2027 EPS growth about -11%).
Defensives that also benefit from lower bond yields.
Selective US consumer exposure that benefits from lower oil and bond yields.
AI capex spillover support fades as capex slows, with risk of de-rating in capex-beneficiary parts.

earnings_insights: GS top-down 2027 EPS growth estimates: S&P 500 11% (from 36% in 2026), STOXX 600 7% (from about 18%), TOPIX 9% (from 24%, FY basis), MSCI AP ex Japan and MSCI EM 26% each.
Consensus (FactSet) 2027E EPS growth: S&P 500 16.5%, STOXX 600 8.4%, TOPIX 13.2%, MSCI AP ex Japan 30.0%, MSCI EM 28.5%, MSCI AC World 17.0%. 2026E EPS growth: S&P 500 32.4%, MSCI AC World 35.6%.

Consensus sector EPS growth 2026E to 2027E: Energy 99.1% to -11.3%, Materials 45.4% to 11.8%, IT 89.2% to 45.3%, Communication Services 33.7% to -5.2%, Health Care 4.4% to 17.7%, Financials 12.3% to 9.3%.
Consensus net margins for the S&P 500 are 16.2% in 2026E and 17.1% in 2027E. For IT they are 29.2% and 31.6%.
Earnings revisions have been unusually positive through 2026, strongest in EM on semiconductor upgrades, and have also risen for 2028 despite the recent sell-off.

GS commodity analysts' forecast, with risks in both directions. WTI is forecast at $78/bbl.
Supports modestly lower bond yields. GS rates forecasts are more dovish than market pricing.
Down from close to its 100th percentile over 20 years, but the US is still the most expensive market.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight US Hyperscalers (long-duration Growth with strong balance sheets)
trade_ideas.rationale: Valuations have fallen sharply and nearly closed the gap with the other 495 S&P 500 stocks, while earnings growth is slower but strong.

trade_ideas.description: Selective cyclical growth: Korean memory and semiconductors
trade_ideas.rationale: Korean memory prices in a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings despite sold-out DRAM and HBM supply through 2029, at 0.7x 2028 P/B.
trade_ideas.risk: High dependence on AI capex, with volatility likely to remain high.

trade_ideas.description: Selective Defensives: US Healthcare, Power and Buyback Aristocrats; Europe Telecoms and Utilities; Asian shareholder-return and secure-dividend strategies
trade_ideas.rationale: Reasonable valuations and benefit from lower bond yields as growth slows.
trade_ideas.risk: Many traditional Defensives no longer look cheap.

trade_ideas.description: Beneficiaries of lower oil and bond yields: US Consumer Discretionary, long-duration Growth, and in Europe Telecoms, Utilities, UK Real Estate, DAX and Retailers; underweight Energy
trade_ideas.rationale: Lower energy costs support real incomes and margins outside Energy, and Europe is the clearest beneficiary as an energy importer.
trade_ideas.risk: Sovereign debt concerns could spike bond yields, especially in Europe.

trade_ideas.description: Regional allocation: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia ex Japan and EM, underweight Europe
trade_ideas.rationale: Based on relative growth, profitability, valuation and risk-adjusted returns.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker AI capex and concentration risk, particularly in Asia.

risk_factors: Bond volatility: sovereign debt concerns could push yields higher, with risk highest in Europe during an election-heavy year. Lower yields would hurt Cyclicals and Financials.
Oil volatility: forecasts carry risks in both directions. Lower oil lifts long-duration Growth but cuts Energy earnings growth, which weighs more on Europe.
Weaker AI capex: slowing capex could de-rate Industrials, memory and chip stocks, and volatility is likely to remain high.
Narrow breadth and momentum concentration in the US and Asia, with higher risk in Asia.
Credit spreads are expected to widen from current levels as growth slows.
Higher cost of capital from inflation-driven policy rates, private-sector capital demand and rising government borrowing.
charts_described: Exhibit 5 shows GS top-down EPS growth for 2026 and 2027: S&P 500 36% to 11%, STOXX 600 18% to 7%, TOPIX 24% to 9%, MSCI AP ex Japan and MSCI EM 26% in 2027.
Exhibit 6 shows hyperscaler capex's estimated contribution to S&P 500 EPS growth: 2pp in 2024, 5pp in 2025, 12pp in 2026, 9pp in 2027 and -5pp in 2028.
vol_and_positioning: GS expects equities to rise in 2027 with higher volatility than in recent years.
MSCI AP ex Japan YTD annualised volatility is 24.2%, the basis for a neutral volatility-adjusted stance on Asia ex Japan and EM.

Index concentration is high: Korea and Taiwan are about half of MSCI EM, with the AI trio (TSMC, Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix) at about 30%. Narrow breadth raises stock-level volatility and momentum-factor risk.
The Value factor sits near the 90th percentile of its 20-year valuation range, and Cyclicals have de-rated sharply versus Defensives.
High dispersion is expected to favor stock-picking, with a focus on stable earnings, strong balance sheets and shareholder returns.
geopolitical: Some normalisation in the Middle East and a recovery in Persian Gulf supply are expected to reduce geopolitical risk premia and bring down commodity prices, including European gas prices.
Fading US tariff effects are cited as a factor lowering inflation.
Europe faces risks from government debt issues and a heavy political calendar, including an election-heavy year.

tension_points.bull_case: De-rated Hyperscalers with strong balance sheets and diversified income, trading at 19.7x, become more valuable as growth slows, and chips and memory offer upside after the sell-off.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler capex growth slows, so AI infrastructure earnings decelerate (IT EPS growth 90% to 45%) and Industrials and chip names face de-rating, with volatility staying high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A faster slowdown or earlier turn in AI capex spending than GS economists expect.

tension_points.bull_case: Brent falls to $78/bbl by end-2027, inflation eases and the Fed and ECB cut in late 2027, supporting long-duration Growth and consumers.
tension_points.bear_case: Sovereign debt concerns could spike bond yields, especially in Europe, and oil risks run in both directions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further spike in bond yields on sovereign debt concerns, or oil staying near $100/bbl rather than falling.
